tools.name: asc__discover_domains
tools.description: List what this server can reach and what it cannot: in profile mode the profiles and sub-profiles that exist, which are loaded here, and how many tools each holds; otherwise the tool domains. Use this when a capability you need is not in the tool list.

tools.name: asc__search_tools
tools.description: Search all App Store Connect operations by keyword, including domains that are not currently loaded. Returns matching tool names, their domain, and the underlying endpoint. Search in English: tool names and descriptions are generated from Apple’s English spec, so translate the goal before searching.

query.description: English keywords to match against tool names, descriptions and paths. A query in another language matches nothing.

tools.name: asc__status
tools.description: Report server configuration, spec version, loaded domains, JWT token state and remaining API rate limit. Also verifies credentials against Apple with a single lightweight request.

check_connection.description: Issue one real API call to verify credentials (default true).

check_expirations.description: Also list signing certificates and provisioning profiles expiring within 30 days (two extra API calls; default false).

check_capabilities.description: Also report what this API key can reach, by probing one cheap endpoint per role family (reports, metadata, reviews, user management, provisioning) and recording ok/forbidden/unauthorized per family — never the role name itself, which no endpoint returns. Up to five extra API calls, fewer when check_connection or check_expirations already covered part of it; default false. Call this once, before relying on a family, rather than discovering the gap from a 403 mid-task.

tools.name: reviews_ai__draft_response
tools.description: Fetch one customer review and return it with an instruction for you to draft a reply — no separate API key needed, you write the text. Returns data only — never posts. Review the draft, then post it yourself with customer_review_responses__create if you approve it.

tools.name: reviews_ai__triage
tools.description: Fetch recent reviews for an app and return them with an instruction for you to group them by theme (bug, feature request, pricing complaint, praise, spam). Read-only.

app_id.description: App ID to triage reviews for.

limit.description: How many recent reviews to pull (default 50, max 200).

unanswered_only.description: Only include reviews without a developer response (default true).

tools.name: reviews_ai__daily_briefing
tools.description: Fetch the last N days of reviews for an app, with volume and rating trend (computed deterministically), and an instruction for you to summarise top complaints, standout praise and one suggested action. Read-only.

tools.name: pricing__set_subscription_price
tools.description: Change or set a subscription price in one territory (country) in a single step. Give it the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID), the subscription (product ID or name), the territory (e.g. TUR, USA) and the price (e.g. "99.99") — it resolves the app, subscription and Apple price point internally and performs the one write. Use this instead of chaining apps__list / subscription_groups / price_points calls when the goal is simply "set/raise/lower the price".

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

subscription.description: Subscription product ID (e.g. com.example.pro.monthly) or its reference name.

territory.description: Territory (country) code, e.g. TUR, USA, DEU.

price.description: Customer price in the territory's currency, e.g. "99.99". Must match an Apple price point exactly; if it does not exist, the nearest available prices are suggested.

preserve_current_price.description: REQUIRED decision about existing subscribers: true = they keep their current price; false = they WILL be moved to the new price. Ask the user if unsure.

start_date.description: Optional start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit to apply as soon as possible.

tools.name: pricing__equalize_price
tools.description: Set one anchor price and let Apple derive the equivalent price in every other country, for an app, an in-app purchase or a subscription. Give the app, which kind of product, the anchor territory (e.g. TUR) and the price (e.g. "99.99"). Apple's own currency and tax maths decides each market — a price is NOT copied across currencies, because 4.99 USD is not 4.99 EUR. REVENUE-level write covering about 175 countries; run it under --dry-run first to see the full derived table.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

product_type.description: What is being priced. "app" is the app's own purchase price, not anything inside it.

product.description: Product ID or reference name of the subscription or in-app purchase. Not used when product_type is "app".

territory.description: The anchor country whose price you are setting, three letters (ISO-3166 alpha-3): TUR, USA, DEU. Every other country is derived from it.

price.description: Customer price in the anchor territory's currency, e.g. "99.99". Must match an Apple price point exactly; the nearest available are suggested if it does not.

preserve_current_price.description: Subscriptions only, and REQUIRED for them: true = existing subscribers keep their current price; false = they WILL be moved to the new one, in every country. Ask the user if unsure.

start_date.description: Optional start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit to apply as soon as possible.

tools.name: pricing__make_offer
tools.description: Make a subscription win-back, promotional or introductory offer, priced in every country where the subscription is sold, in one call. Give the app, the subscription, the offer kind, mode, duration and periods, and either an anchor territory and price or a free trial. Every other market comes from Apple's own equalizations of the anchor. Win-back and promotional offers go to Apple as one request, so they exist complete or not at all. Introductory offers are one write per country, taking a few minutes: everything is checked first, it stops at the first failure, and the same call again resumes. Once made, only an introductory offer's end date can change. Refuses without writing when any country is missing a price. REVENUE-level write; run it under --dry-run first to see the full derived table.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

subscription.description: Subscription product ID (e.g. com.example.pro.yearly) or its reference name.

offer_type.description: win_back: shown to lapsed subscribers who meet the eligibility below. promotional: redeemed by existing or lapsed subscribers through a signed offer in the app. introductory: the first period for customers new to the subscription group.

name.description: Win-back and promotional, required: reference name, seen only in App Store Connect.

offer_id.description: Win-back and promotional, required: the identifier the app uses for this offer (Apple's offerId for win-back, offerCode for promotional). Must not be used by any other offer of this subscription.

offer_mode.description: PAY_AS_YOU_GO: the price is charged every period, for `periods` periods. PAY_UP_FRONT: the price is charged once for the whole duration. FREE_TRIAL: no price; leave territory and price out.

duration.description: Length of one offer period (PAY_AS_YOU_GO) or of the whole offer.

periods.description: Number of periods. 1 for PAY_UP_FRONT and FREE_TRIAL.

territory.description: Paid offers: the anchor country, three letters (ISO-3166 alpha-3): TUR, USA, DEU. Every other country is derived from it.

price.description: Paid offers: customer price in the anchor territory's currency, e.g. "29.99". Must match an Apple price point exactly; the nearest available are suggested if it does not.

eligibility_paid_months.description: Win-back only, required: how many months the customer must have paid for before.

eligibility_last_subscribed_min_months.description: Win-back only, required: fewest months since the customer's subscription lapsed.

eligibility_last_subscribed_max_months.description: Win-back only, required: most months since the customer's subscription lapsed.

eligibility_wait_months.description: Win-back only, optional: months before the same customer can redeem this offer again.

start_date.description: First day the offer runs (YYYY-MM-DD). Required for win-back; optional for introductory (omit to start now); not used for promotional.

end_date.description: The offer's end date (YYYY-MM-DD), win-back and introductory only. Omit for open-ended.

undo.description: Introductory only. true takes back an introductory offer this tool set: with the same terms, price and dates as the original call, it deletes that exact offer in every country carrying it, one country at a time, and touches no other offer.

priority.description: Win-back only: how Apple ranks it against other offers. Defaults to NORMAL.

tools.name: pricing__get_subscription_price
tools.description: What a subscription costs customers today — in one country, or in every country at once. Give the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID); both other arguments are optional. Omit the territory to get worldwide pricing, grouped by price so the answer stays readable, with the currency and the country codes in each group. Omit the subscription to cover every subscription in the app, which is how you answer "what does the weekly one cost" without knowing its product ID. Use this instead of chaining apps__list / subscription_groups / prices calls. It also returns the price actually in effect: subscriptions__prices__list returns price-less stubs unless the caller knows to include the price point.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

territory.description: Optional. Territory (country) code — three letters, ISO-3166 alpha-3: USA, TUR, DEU. Omit it for every country Apple sells in (about 175), grouped by price.

subscription.description: Optional. Product ID or reference name. Omit to return every subscription in the app.

tools.name: pricing__get_iap_price
tools.description: Read current and scheduled in-app purchase prices by territory, including currency, customer price, proceeds, dates, and manual or automatic source. Give an IAP ID, or give the app and IAP product ID. Omit territory for all countries.

app.description: App name, bundle ID or Apple ID; required with a product ID.

iap.description: In-app purchase ID (without app) or product ID (with app).

territory.description: Optional three-letter country code, e.g. TUR, USA.

tools.name: pricing__set_iap_price
tools.description: Change or set an in-app purchase (IAP) price in one territory (country) without assembling a price schedule. Give an IAP ID, or the app and IAP product ID, plus the territory (e.g. TUR) and the price (e.g. "99.99"). Apple replaces an IAP price schedule as a whole, so every other manual price and scheduled change is read and re-sent unchanged. Pricing the base territory also moves Apple's automatic prices elsewhere. REVENUE-level write.

app.description: App name, bundle ID or Apple ID; required with a product ID.

iap.description: In-app purchase ID (without app) or product ID (with app).

territory.description: Three-letter country code, e.g. TUR, USA.

price.description: Customer price in the territory's currency, e.g. "99.99". Must match an Apple price point exactly; the nearest available are suggested if it does not.

start_date.description: Optional start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Omit to apply as soon as possible.

tools.name: pricing__get_app_price
tools.description: Read current and scheduled app purchase prices by territory, including currency, customer price, proceeds, dates, and manual or automatic source. Omit territory for all countries.

app.description: App name, bundle ID or Apple ID.

territory.description: Optional three-letter country code, e.g. TUR, USA.

tools.name: listing__get_screenshots
tools.description: List the screenshots on an app’s store listing in one step: which locales have them, which device sizes, how many, and their dimensions. Give the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID). Use this instead of chaining app_store_versions / localizations / screenshot_sets / screenshots — most locales carry no screenshots of their own, so walking that chain costs one call per locale.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

locale.description: Optional. Restrict to one locale, e.g. en-US or tr.

version.description: Optional version string, e.g. "2.4". Defaults to the most recent version.

tools.name: listing__upload_screenshot
tools.description: Upload a screenshot image file to an app’s store listing in one step. Give the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID), the locale, the device size and a path to the file on this machine. Handles Apple’s reserve/upload/commit sequence and the checksum — the raw screenshot tool reserves a slot and moves no bytes. PUBLIC-level write: the image appears on the store listing once Apple processes it.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

locale.description: Listing locale the screenshot belongs to, e.g. en-US or tr.

display_type.description: Device size the image is sized for, e.g. APP_IPHONE_67. A wrong one is rejected by Apple on commit, not on upload.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the PNG or JPEG on this machine.

version.description: Optional version string, e.g. "2.4". Defaults to the most recent version.

tools.name: listing__upload_asset
tools.description: Upload an image or video file into an app’s asset library in one step, and optionally place it on a store page in the same call. Give the app, the file path and the category; to place it, add a placement type and either a locale (the version page) or the id of a custom product page, experiment or in-app event localization. Handles Apple’s reserve/upload/commit sequence, which the raw library tools cannot finish. PUBLIC-level write when it places the file; the upload alone shows nowhere.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a PNG or JPEG image, or an MP4 or MOV video, on this machine.

category.description: What the file is for in the library.

reference_name.description: Optional name to find the file by in the library. Defaults to the file name.

preview_frame_time_code.description: Videos only, optional: the frame shown before playback, e.g. "00:00:05:00".

placement_type.description: Optional. Place the uploaded file as this. Leave out to upload without placing.

placement_group.description: Optional placement group, e.g. a device class. The allowed groups per type come from the asset library reference data.

locale.description: Place on this locale of the version page, e.g. en-US or tr.

version.description: With locale: version string, e.g. "2.4". Defaults to the most recent version.

custom_product_page_localization_id.description: Place on this custom product page localization instead.

experiment_treatment_localization_id.description: Place on this product page optimization treatment localization instead.

app_event_localization_id.description: Place on this in-app event localization instead.

tools.name: listing__delete_assets
tools.description: Delete images or videos from an app’s asset library. One confirmation covers them all and names each file. Give the app and the ids of the files; every id is checked against that app’s library before anything is deleted. DESTRUCTIVE-level write: deletion is not reversible.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

asset_ids.description: Ids of the library images or videos to delete, from the library’s image and video lists.

tools.name: analytics__get_report
tools.description: Read an App Store analytics report as rows, in one step. Give the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID) and the report name or category; it walks the request → report → instance → segment chain, downloads the gzipped TSV Apple stores behind a signed link, and returns decoded rows. Use this instead of chaining analytics_report_requests / analytics_reports / analytics_report_instances / analytics_report_segments, which ends holding a URL rather than data. Does not start a new report request.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

report.description: Report name, exact or partial, e.g. "App Store Installations". Omit to list what this app has available instead of downloading one.

category.description: Narrow the report search to one category.

granularity.description: Which cadence of instance to read. Defaults to DAILY.

processing_date.description: Instance date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the most recent instance Apple has processed, which is usually not today.

max_rows.description: Cap on returned data rows (default 200, hard cap 1000).

tools.name: ci__diagnose_run
tools.description: Diagnose why an Xcode Cloud build failed in one call. Give an app name, bundle ID or Apple ID; optionally a build run ID or number and a workflow name or ID. By default inspect the newest run whose completionStatus is FAILED or ERRORED (canceled and skipped runs are passed over) (within the newest 40 runs). Returns failing actions, issues and failed tests, with bounded counts and truncation notes. Read-only.

app.description: App name, bundle ID or numeric Apple ID.

run.description: Build run ID or run number. Omit for the newest failed or errored run.

workflow.description: Workflow name or ID to narrow the run search.

tools.name: preflight__check_version
tools.description: Check whether an app version is complete enough to submit, in one call, and list what is missing. Give the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID). Verifies the build is attached and finished processing, the export compliance answer is given, the review contact and demo account are filled in, every locale has a description and keywords, and screenshots exist. Each gap names the tool that fixes it. Read-only — it changes nothing and does not submit.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

version.description: Version string (e.g. "3.2.0"). Defaults to the newest version that is still editable.

platform.description: Which platform’s version. Needed when the app has one on more than one platform.

tools.name: preflight__check_subscription
tools.description: Check subscription catalog readiness before submitting for review. Give the app and either a subscription (product ID, name or ID) or a group (reference name or ID). Checks localizations, group locales, prices, plan availability, review screenshot, review note and required attributes; reports state and blocking or warning findings with the raw tool that fixes each gap. Group mode checks at most 20 subscriptions. All reads are capped and truncation is reported. Read-only; ready means no observed blocking catalog gaps, not a prediction of Apple approval or permission to submit.

app.description: App name, bundle ID or numeric Apple ID.

subscription.description: Exact product ID, name or subscription ID. Cannot be combined with group.

group.description: Exact reference name or group ID. Check up to 20 subscriptions in this group.

tools.name: listing__diff_metadata
tools.description: Compare the store text of two app versions locale by locale, in one call, and list only what differs. Give the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID). By default it compares the version that is on sale against the one being prepared, which is the answer to "what am I about to change?". Reports per locale which of description, keywords, whatsNew, promotional text, marketing URL and support URL changed, plus locales added or dropped. Read-only.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

from.description: Version string to compare from. Defaults to the version on sale.

to.description: Version string to compare to. Defaults to the version being prepared.

locale.description: Restrict to one locale (e.g. "en-US", "tr"). Omit to compare every locale.

tools.name: asc__account_status
tools.description: Show every app in the account with the version that is live, the version in flight, and whose move it is — in one call. Translates App Store states into the action they imply: approved-and-held apps, rejections, submissions stuck on export compliance, and versions never submitted. Also opens each app's review submission, so an in-app purchase or event Apple rejected shows up even when the version itself reads as fine. Start here when the question is "what needs my attention?" rather than one app. Read-only.

only_actionable.description: Return only the apps waiting on you, dropping the ones where nothing is pending or Apple has the ball (default false).

tools.name: metadata_ai__audit_localizations
tools.description: Compare an app version’s store text across every language and report what is missing or over Apple’s limit — empty descriptions, blank keywords, fields present in one language and absent in others. Read-only: it reports and stops, and never fills anything in.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

version.description: Version string (e.g. "3.2.0"). Defaults to the newest version.

tools.name: metadata_ai__draft_translation
tools.description: Return one language’s store text plus an instruction for you to draft it in the languages named. Only runs for locales the caller asks for — it never decides that a language looks stale. Returns a draft for a person to read; writing is a separate step, and for keywords the draft is a starting point rather than an answer, because keywords are a search-ranking choice rather than a translation.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

from_locale.description: Source language to translate from, e.g. "en-US".

to_locales.description: Target languages, e.g. ["tr", "de-DE"]. Required and never inferred: translating a language nobody asked about is how a deliberate choice gets overwritten.

fields.description: Which fields to draft. Defaults to description and whatsNew. One of: description, keywords, whatsNew, promotionalText, marketingUrl, supportUrl.

version.description: Version string. Defaults to the newest version.

tools.name: metadata_ai__apply_localizations
tools.description: Write store text for several languages at once from a file the user prepared — the values are theirs, read straight from the file rather than retyped. Accepts CSV with a "locale" column and one column per field, or JSON keyed by locale. Every value is checked against Apple’s character limits before anything is sent, so a file with a bad value changes nothing at all. Apple is still asked one language at a time: if it rejects the eleventh, the first ten are already written and the error names exactly which ones landed.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

file_path.description: Path to the CSV or JSON file. CSV: a header row of "locale" plus any of description, keywords, whatsNew, promotionalText, marketingUrl, supportUrl. JSON: {"tr": {"description": "…"}, "de-DE": {…}}.

version.description: Version string. Defaults to the newest version.

tools.name: release__submit
tools.description: Send an App Store version to Apple for review in one call — it opens the submission, puts the version in it, and hands it over. Checks first that the version is actually submittable and refuses rather than submitting something that will bounce. Use this instead of opening an empty review submission by hand, which by itself sends nothing.

app.description: App name, bundle ID (com.example.app) or numeric Apple ID.

version.description: Version string (e.g. "3.2.0"). Defaults to the newest editable version.

platform.description: Which platform’s version. Needed when the app has one on more than one platform.

skip_preflight.description: Submit even when the pre-flight finds blocking gaps. Off by default, and worth leaving off: every gap it reports is one Apple enforces.

tools.name: testflight__assign_build_to_groups
tools.description: Assign one processed, unexpired TestFlight build to named beta groups. Checks existing assignments and reports each group, including partial failures. External groups may need beta app review before testers can install the build. RELEASE-level write.

app.description: App name, bundle ID, or numeric Apple ID.

build.description: Exact build number (Apple build version) or build ID. Required; ambiguous matches are refused.

groups.description: Exact beta group names or IDs.

tools.name: testflight__feedback_digest
tools.description: Summarize what TestFlight beta testers are reporting: recent crash and screenshot feedback grouped by build version, counts, top devices and OS versions, newest comments, and short crash log excerpts. Give the app (name, bundle ID or Apple ID), optionally a build number or UUID and days (default 14, max 90). Reads at most five pages of 50 submissions per type, ten comments per type per build, and three crash logs (first 40 lines or 4 KB each). Reports truncation. Read-only.

app.description: App name, bundle ID or numeric Apple ID.

build.description: Build number (including numeric timestamps) or build UUID. Omit for all builds.

   app → group → subscription → price chain. Prefer it over walking the chain.
